articles.title: Unstoppable Luka Doncic makes a strong demand of teammates amid league-wide domination: “I think we have the potential for that”
articles.summary: Luka Doncic had five steals and two blocks in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, yet he still wants the team to defend
articles.body: Luka Doncic had five steals and two blocks in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, yet he still wants the team to defend better. He returned after missing Sunday’s game with lower back tightness and finished with 32 points, 10 assists and eight rebounds.Los Angeles has won six straight and sits at 10-2, but Doncic pointed to the one number he did not like. The Lakers entered Monday ranked 21st in defensive efficiency, a spot he believes is well below what the roster can reach.What did Luka Doncic say about the Lakers’ defense?Doncic told reporters the Lakers can climb well past 21st. “I think we have the potential for that,” he said.His own night backed up the point. The Lakers guard did a lot of the damage with his hands, and the team finished with 16 steals, three from Matisse Thybulle and two from Ziaire Williams. Those takeaways turned into 29 points while Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (right finger sprain) sat out. Los Angeles also blocked six shots, two of them by Doncic.Atlanta still found ways to score. The Hawks hit 17 of 44 from 3-point range and grabbed 12 offensive rebounds to the Lakers’ eight, though those boards produced only eight second-chance points, two fewer than Los Angeles got. CJ McCollum and Aaron Wiggins combined for 36 points off Atlanta’s bench. The Lakers gave up 35 points in the second quarter and 33 in the third. They led by as many as 20 and won by 10.At 10-2 with the 21st-ranked defense, the Lakers are winning on offense and takeaways. Doncic is asking the rest of the game to catch up.Doncic’s 45-point week earned Western Conference honorsThe NBA named the guard Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Nov. 2 to 8. It was the fifth time he has won the award with Los Angeles and the 20th in his career. Doncic averaged 45.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 8.3 assists on 52.5% shooting from the field and 39.5% from 3-point range, and the Lakers won all three games he played.He opened with 42 points and 13 assists in a 138-117 win over Miami, then scored 40 in a 116-103 victory at Sacramento. His season-high 53 came in a 124-118 NBA Cup win over Portland, which put him with Elgin Baylor, George Mikan and Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers to score 40 or more in four straight games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s $25 million commitment makes an impact as their foundation reaches over 7,000 Oakland students
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have tirelessly worked towards the communities in Oakland that they have been able
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have tirelessly worked towards the communities in Oakland that they have been able to build through their own efforts over the last decade. As the four time NBA champion remains on a winning streak at court, their foundation, Eat, Learn & Play has marked a new milestone.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation marks a milestone in Oakland as they remain committed to studentsA few days ago, Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play took to their social media to make a post that read as, “7 Years of Investing in Oakland Students✨ When a child learns to read, everything changes. Curiosity takes off, and a whole world opens up. That’s why, in 2024, Eat. Learn. Play. pledged $25 million over five years to close Oakland’s literacy gap, working toward 10,000 tutoring opportunities by 2029.”Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play’s post added, “To date, our 1:1 and small group tutoring has reached over 7,500 students in the Oakland Unified School District. Personalized support layered on top of classroom instruction with students building confidence one page at a time. We’ve also placed more than 1 million books into Oakland kids’ hands with the @Oaklitcoalition and through programs like our free holiday book boxes and book fairs, and the Eat. Learn. Play. Bus.”Ever since the foundation was set up in 2016, Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry’s main focus has been the wellbeing of children in Oakland.The primary mission of their foundation, Eat, Learn & Play has been to give access to quality education to children of all age groups in Oakland, provide quality meals to them and also encourage them to take active interest in sports.The four time NBA champion’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, has changed thousands of lives across Oakland as both Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have continued to be there for the children belonging to their hometown.The two also recently collaborated with billionaire investor Warren Buffet to raise a whopping $7.1 million for the children of Oakland.Stephen Curry’s Golden State Warriors remains unbeatable on the field in the new seasonAfter an injury plagued season, the four time NBA champion has bounced back well on the field.As per reports, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry is averaging 30.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game while shooting 50.3% from the field and 45.7% from three-point range for the Golden State Warriors in the 2026–27 NBA season.The team has been on a winning streak for the last eight games and it has sparked chaos.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joel Embiid injury update: Latest on Sixers star after awkward fall during high-stakes against Celtics
articles.summary: Joel Embiid went down hard in the closing seconds of the first half as the Sixers chased the Celtics on Tuesday night.
articles.body: Joel Embiid went down hard in the closing seconds of the first half as the Sixers chased the Celtics on Tuesday night. The center missed a transition layup, slipped on the landing and rolled over in pain. Embiid got up and ran back on defense, but the limp was easy to see. Boston also led by double digits at the break, and the Sixers need Embiid to find a rhythm after a rough start to his season. Both teams entered as the top two in the East, which made the scare hard to ignore.What happened to Joel Embiid against the Celtics?Boston won the first quarter 30-23 and kept pushing in the second, so Philadelphia was already behind before the fall. Embiid went up for a transition layup and missed. A slip of the right foot on the landing sent the big man crashing, and the planted left foot tweaked the ankle. The quarter ended seconds later, and Embiid limped to the locker room for halftime.The news after the break was better. Embiid returned to start the third quarter and snapped the shooting slump with a three-pointer. Neither moment settles how the ankle feels, and no further word on it had come out at that stage.Asked what felt off after Sunday’s win over the Bulls, Embiid answered with one word, everything, and framed the fix this way: “Figuring out how to just be myself again.”Shooting slump adds to the early concernThe first half was rough even before the fall. Embiid played 17 minutes and missed all six shots from the field, two of them from three. The nine points all came at the line, where Embiid hit nine of 11 attempts. Five rebounds and two turnovers rounded out the half.Sunday against the Bulls was little better from the floor. Embiid went 7-for-19, missed both three-point tries and dropped to 3-for-30 from deep this season. The center did grab 10 rebounds, eight on the offensive glass, but most were cleanups of Embiid’s own misses.Injuries have defined Embiid’s NBA career so far, and the main fear around this Sixers season was a physical issue cutting it short. A fall like this one brings that fear back. A hobbled Embiid would hurt Philadelphia’s chances of coming back in this game and holding its place at the top of the East.Philadelphia has Tyrese Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe, LeBron James, and Jaylen Brown around Embiid, and a 9-2 start shows the team can win while the big man searches for form.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tatum's Celtics Beat Brown's 76ers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for LeBron, George, Top Players
articles.summary: The main storyline ahead of Tuesday's Philadelphia 76ers vs. Boston Celtics matchup was the drama brewing between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum. Their pregame "greeting" added a few more logs to the fire.
articles.body:
The main storyline ahead of Tuesday's Philadelphia 76ers vs. Boston Celtics matchup was the drama brewing between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum. Their pregame "greeting" added a few more logs to the fire.

But the Celtics quickly shot that narrative into the background.

Celtics' Shootaround Song Ahead of Tatum vs. Brown 🌶️

Behind Boston's red-hot shooting and some foul trouble from Brown, the Celtics rolled to a 123-101 win over the Sixers in the first matchup between the rivals this season.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

The Celtics staged a full blitzkrieg from beyond the arc on Tuesday night, finishing 22-of-49 from three. It was a pure expression of Joe Mazzulla ball.

The Sixers struggled from beyond the arc, meanwhile, finishing just 11-of-37 from three. That discrepancy in perimeter shooting played an enormous role in Boston's victory.

And while much of the pregame hype centered on Brown vs. Tatum, it was Paul George who truly had a memorable revenge game, torching his former team.

Tuesday was a case study in how the Celtics (9-2) want to win—spread the floor, hit a bunch of threes, play good defense. It's a difficult formula to deal with when the threes are falling at a high rate.

For the Sixers (9-3), meanwhile, it was a reminder that the halfcourt offense remains a work in progress, though it was also just a poor shooting night. Boston's defense certainly contributed to that, and the barrage of threes gave the Sixers less chances to steal easy buckets in transition, a hallmark of their success to this point.

These teams will play three more times this season, though the next matchup won't be until Jan. 21. Round 1 went to the Celtics in resounding fashion.

articles.title: Bryce James' Box Score Stats, Highlights from Arizona's Win vs. Northern Arizona
articles.summary: Bryce James made his third appearance of the 2026-27 season during Arizona's 90-59 win over Northern Arizona on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Bryce James made his third appearance of the 2026-27 season during Arizona's 90-59 win over Northern Arizona on Tuesday night.

James, the son of Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James, played 13 minutes in the blowout victory.

New 2027 Men's NCAA Tournament Bracket Projections 🔮

Arizona didn't face much resistance during the contest, jumping out to a 23-9 lead to open the game.

The Wildcats excelled on both ends of the floor throughout the first half, holding a 46-22 edge at halftime.

Northern Arizona started to cut into the deficit by beginning the second half on an 18-11 run, but Arizona quickly responded with an 18-3 run of its own to gain a 32-point advantage.

The younger James was previously held scoreless across six minutes in his season debut on Nov. 2, but scored five points and picked up two steals while shooting 2-of-5 from the field during Arizona's 104-84 victory over Cal Poly on Thursday.

The 19-year-old previously spent the 2025-26 season with the Wildcats, but chose to redshirt as a freshman before entering their rotation this year.

James will be back in action when Arizona travels to face Auburn on Friday. Tip-off is at 9 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown repeatedly snubs ex-teammate Jayson Tatum as Celtics crush Sixers 'lambchops and some gravy'
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown gave Jayson Tatum the cold shoulder before tip-off in Philly, capping months of silence after a tense dinner confrontation in France.
articles.body: Former Celtics All-Star Jaylen Brown confronted ex-running mate Jayson Tatum at a dinner table in France last June over their future in Boston, and that bad blood finally resurfaced on the hardwood Tuesday night. According to ESPN insider Shams Charania, that awkward European sit-down marked the last time the two stars spoke face-to-face. GIANNIS ANTETOKOUNMPO ERA TO END IN MILWAUKEE AS BUCKS WILL SEND TWO-TIME MVP TO MIAMI HEAT FOR YOUNG CORE Boston had just struck out on Giannis Antetokounmpo, who ended up in Miami instead. Celtics brass had put Brown on the table in those talks. Once Brown caught wind he was being shopped, he went straight to Tatum to find out where he stood and whether Tatum still wanted him in Boston. Charania reported that Brown approached and confronted Tatum at the dinner table specifically to address their future as a tandem and gauge where Tatum stood on the entire situation. Boston traded Brown to Philadelphia days later, effectively ending communication between the two. Tatum called and texted, but Brown never answered. JAYLEN BROWN SOUNDS LIKE A 'SORE LOSER' AFTER BLAMING EMBIID FOR CELTICS' COLLAPSE Seconds before tip-off Tuesday night in Philly, Tatum walked over and tapped Brown on the chest to say hello. Brown gave him absolute zero back. Eyes locked dead ahead, Brown didn't flinch, didn't dap him up, and blew right past him like Tatum wasn't there. Asked before Tuesday's tip if he planned to clear the air, Brown said, "There's nothing to talk about." Brown then dropped the first on-court faceoff between the two, as Philadelphia fell 123-101 to Boston. After the final buzzer, Brown hugged several of his former teammates before heading back to the locker room, leaving the floor without saying a word to Tatum. Brown had 13 points against his former team. Tatum had 21 on 8-for-17 shooting. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! When Tatum claimed on video last month that the trade caught him off guard, Brown hit back on Instagram with a blue cap emoji. Tatum tried shutting down the drama to reporters: "This ain't no f---ing Shaq and Kobe. There's no beef." Brown countered on camera: "I saw that he said it's no beef and I think he's right. There's no beef. Jayson comes from a wonderful family. We've accomplished some great things. He's a hell of a basketball player. He's got a great PR team. It's no beef. But it might be a little lambchops and some gravy." Drafted third overall in back-to-back drafts (Brown in 2016, Tatum in 2017), the duo reached five conference finals, two NBA Finals and won the 2024 NBA title. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Debates over franchise ownership followed. Tatum earned First Team All-NBA nods, while Brown won the 2024 Eastern Conference Finals MVP and Finals MVP awards. articles.title: Jaylen Brown snubbed Jayson Tatum before tipoff. His night against the Celtics only got worse
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown's emotional reunion with Jayson Tatum couldn't have gone much worse. And his struggles against Boston may be a sign of a much bigger problem in...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The final blow to the 76ers' chest — and their ego — came with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, as Paul George held his follow-through in front of his former bench and Jayson Tatum stretched his wings toward his teammate in celebration.

In stark contrast, Jaylen Brown's confusion over a busted coverage was plastered all over his face as he and the veteran, star-studded bunch shuffled back to their seats before the white flag was raised. What should have been a hotly contested duel had flamed out rather quickly, with hundreds of fans heading for the exits and a blowout in full effect.

"I'm a bit frustrated, honestly," Brown said following the 123-101 defeat . "I wanted to perform better for my team. Foul trouble kind of derailed me a little bit, but it happens. It's unfortunate but you gotta just move on to the next."

For weeks, the sheer build-up to Tuesday night essentially guaranteed an emotional apex. Cryptic messages, subtle shots and narratives built on both sides of the Tatum-Brown divide dominated headlines, airwaves and basketball discourse. Something was bound to give.

But even in that, Brown's emotions quite possibly got the best of him. Seconds before tipoff, after the tidal wave of boos, tension and apprehension had consumed the building, Brown had a golden opportunity to bury the hatchet as Tatum approached him near midcourt. An embrace, nod or handshake — something to acknowledge the near-decade relationship between the two — was set up perfectly. Instead, Brown chose in that moment to ignore Tatum as he tapped his former teammate's arm and chest twice.

It didn't end there. Brown used every opportunity he had to latch onto Tatum like an All-Pro cornerback, at times not even recognizing the ongoing action around him. When he received the ball, he put his head down and charged at opposing defenders recklessly, unable to generate rhythm — and the rampant roars from the Philly faithful only compounded Brown's downhill desperation and aggression. (Brown recorded his second-highest first-quarter usage rate this season, paired poorly with a 28.6 turnover rate.) A failure to find an offensive groove carried over to the other side of the ball, with Brown giving away cheap fouls, forcing him to sit and ultimately limiting him to just 25 minutes. His final tally told the story better than anything else could: 13 points, four turnovers and a game-worst minus-27.

"I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else was, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed and shot the hell out of the ball. They were the better team tonight."

To add insult to injury, it was Tatum and George who looked like they had played for nine years together instead of the three weeks. Boston has found a way to harmonize the pair's similar skill sets, as both combine usage ( 100th and 91st percentiles , respectively) with creation chops (98th and 87th percentiles). One of George's underrepresented qualities is his ability to assimilate within different ecosystems while not detracting from the order of operations. The Celtics have outscored opponents by 33 points in the 162 minutes both have shared the floor, a promising early sign for the league's No. 2 team in net rating. Both George and Tatum can play off the other, whether it's darting around screens and relocating, spacing the floor or drawing defenses to one side of the floor. The pair accounted for 18 of Boston's 49 attempted 3s, a hand-in-glove fit for Mazzulla ball — in addition to 56 points, 9 treys, 11 rebounds and 5 assists, feasting upon their prey. Beef. Lamb chops. Gravy.

For Brown, the conversation will continue surrounding how the former Finals MVP truly fits within the 76ers' structure. And it's not just that he's converting shots and handling the ball at rates not seen in over seven years , it's that his entire offensive makeup has changed drastically. Last season — the campaign Brown notoriously proclaimed as his favorite of his career — he operated as a lead ball-handler nearly 25 percent of the time on the floor, per Synergy tracking data. That volume has plummeted to just seven percent, with the bulk of his opportunities coming via spot-ups or in transition. Brown is certainly not as fluid or creative a playmaker as his former teammate Tatum or even George, but the sudden removal of opportunities certainly comes with its own trickle-down effects.

"He had a tough night," 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said. "They did a pretty good job of swarming him and sending multiple defenders."

The larger theme, one that will permeate this game, a rematch in Boston (which will be even more emotional for Brown) and beyond, is the fact that the 76ers' presumed path to playing in May and June also includes the Celtics. Both sit atop the Eastern Conference, having won nine games apiece, with some underlying separation already building on the coast. (Detroit and New York will certainly have something to say about how the final standings shake out; early November is a far cry from finality, but I'm more confident in seeing the demarcation between them and the likes of Toronto, Miami and Atlanta.)

It's why nights like these are important. They offer a window into the psyche of the world's most talented athletes, invoke emotional and mental challenges and push conversations forward. Brown will have more opportunities to even the score against his old coworker, but until he fully settles into his new surroundings, frustrating outings like this won't be outliers.

articles.title: NBA: Boston Celtics best LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers as Jaylen Brown shares frosty reunion with former team
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics secured a huge 123-101 road win against LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers to go top of the Eastern Conference; watch the 2026/27 NBA season, including the Christmas Day games and the NBA finals, on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Brown ran into early foul trouble and scored only 13 points in his first game against Boston since the 2024 NBA Finals MVP was traded over the summer to the Sixers. His head-to-head showdown with Tatum was one of the more anticipated early-season matchups with both players refusing to say much about their frosty relationship.

Tatum tried to dap up Brown before the opening tip with a tap on the shoulder and thump on the chest that his former teammate ignored. Tatum shook hands and exchanged a big hug with LeBron James.

Brown picked up two quick fouls in the first quarter and was whistled for his fourth early in the second half.

George, traded for Brown after two seasons with the 76ers, enjoyed the homecoming. He appeared to give the finger in a bowling motion near the visitor's bench after he sank his fourth 3 of the game for a 100-82 lead that pushed the Celtics to their ninth win in 10 games.

The Sixers survived a scare late in the second half when Joel Embiid landed awkwardly and hit the court on a missed layup attempt. The oft-injured big man curled up on the court while VJ Edgecombe dunked over him.

Embiid gingerly ran down the court and hunched over as the halftime horn sounded with the Celtics up 62-51.

Embiid's health has been a career-long issue for him, and the Sixers have declined to play him in back-to-back games. A two-time NBA scoring champion, Embiid has slumped with his shot this season, with no game worse than last Friday in Cleveland when missed all nine shots from the floor and scored only two points.

He had missed 27 of 30 (and 20 consecutive) 3-pointers entering the game. Embiid missed two 3-point attempts in the first half but opened the second with his first 3 since the second game of the season.

Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 24 points.

No love lost for Brown as Celtics new order dominate

Brown wasn't a fan of Tatum's brief show of affection, as mentioned above, perhaps a fitting illustration of a frosty relationship that has included radio silence between the two All-Stars since Brown was traded in the summer to the Sixers.

Tatum scored 21 points and outplayed Brown, while George - who the Sixers traded to acquire Brown in the summer - was the star of the night, scoring 14 straight points in the fourth quarter and making six of Boston's 22 3-pointers.

"No headlines about anything like that," Tatum said. "I was just getting ready for the game. Ready for jump ball. Go out there and compete and have some fun and try and get the win."

Brown ran into early foul trouble and scored only 13 points in his first game against Boston since the 2024 NBA Finals MVP was traded. He picked up two quick fouls in the first quarter and was whistled for his fourth early in the second half.

Brown declined to get into his Tatum brush off.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else was just, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention."

articles.title: Hamilton state champion diver aims for NCAA title, picks national power
articles.summary: Josi Popma has been one of the best divers in the state. She has made her college decision where she hopes to be one of the country's best.
articles.body:
HAMILTON - Josi Popma might be one of the shortest on the pool deck, but she has delivered some of the biggest performances.

The senior diver stands just 4 feet, 10 inches, but as the defending Division 3 state champion she is setting a giant legacy at Hamilton.

"It definitely puts a lot of pressure on, but I just have to keep doing what I do," Popma said. "I think my height is an advantage because I can spin really fast - I just have to keep it controlled. It gives me confidence because I know I have done it before."

She has done plenty this season, too. Popma broke the Hamilton pool, school and OK Lakeshore Conference record on Saturday, Nov. 7, with a score of 490.15.

"I have been working on my takeoffs and getting higher on my dives," she said.

Hamilton coach Aaron Paskvan said she has become a well-rounded athlete this year.

"Her maturity has been the biggest thing this year. She makes the adjustments and the leadership comes with the maturity," he said. "Her special awareness has helped (team with her fast spins) to feel her spots on her dives."

Popma's performance and potential has received plenty of attention from bigger schools, too.

This week, she made her decision and committed to dive at Grand Valley State.

"I liked the environment of the team. They have really good divers and it felt really welcoming," Popma said. "It just felt like my place to be. It means a lot. I have worked so hard to get there. It is awesome to see that hard work pay off."

The Lakers have a history of great diving, including multiple NCAA champions in recent years.

"It makes me hope that I can get there one day (and win a national title) with some more years of training," Popma said. "I am really excited to see what I can do."

articles.title: Vote now among 21 nominees for StarNews preseason boys basketball player of the year
articles.summary: Vote now for the Wilmington-area high school boys basketball preseason player of the year.
articles.body:
The 2026 North Carolina high school boys basketball season has already arrived as teams across the state can begin action as early as Wednesday, Nov. 11.

Wilmington-area teams enter this winter on the heels of a dazzling 2025-26 season that saw two Port City squads battle for a regional championship and one come just short of a state title.

But the 2026-27 season is a reset for many teams that graduated skilled senior classes. While there may be some new faces, don't be fooled: Wilmington still has plenty of basketball star power.

Now fans have a chance to voice their opinion by voting in the 2026 StarNews Boys Basketball Preseason Player of the Year Poll, which includes 21 nominees from each of the area's 13 squads.

Voting in this poll is fan driven and will run until Tuesday., Nov. 24, at 11:59 p.m. Vote now as many times as you like below.
